outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: None that matter here (e.g., whether the listing is labeled “latest-posts” vs “More from Search Engine Land” is just a UI/URL detail).

Critical issues: (1) The agent never provided the required deliverable (title, publication date, and author). Its final output is only an error message. (2) There is no evidence the agent actually reached the earliest available article on the site or even an end-of-pagination/oldest-page boundary. Screenshots show the agent paginating through pages 4–10 of a “More from Search Engine Land” feed with articles dated in mid/late 2026 (e.g., Jul 21, 2026; Aug 26, 2026), which are clearly not “earliest available” for a long-running publication. (3) The claimed blocker (“timed out after 90 seconds”) is not corroborated by the final screenshots, which show normal content pages loaded; regardless, even if a timeout occurred, the agent did not report the oldest-accessible article’s title/date/author before stopping.

Outcome assessment: The agent made some on-site effort by paginating to older pages, but it did not identify the earliest available article and did not report the required metadata. From an average user’s perspective, the task was not completed because the user received no earliest-article result at all.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the single earliest (oldest) article that is available on Search Engine Land, along with its title, publication date, and author. A reasonable user would be flexible about how the agent finds it (pagination, sitemap, search, etc.), but not flexible about missing the required metadata or failing to actually identify an earliest/oldest article.
